candidates.detail: resolved_plan_overlap_area multiplies, on the left solid axes, max(0, left half-extent + projected right half-extent - absolute center separation). That expression is a separation margin, not the length of the intersection when one interval lies inside another; it can overstate area even with equal zero yaw. The finite nonnegative Area wrapper admits the computed number but does not establish that it equals contact area. The breteche roof-bearing audit requires the returned area for each support/plate pair to be at least 0.014 square metres and also checks height, support role and a sampled point.
candidates.source_derived_case: For a conditional 2 m straight run with zero yaw, the generator places an inner plate of plan dimensions 2.18 by 0.18 m and a post of 0.18 by 0.18 m at x=0.62 relative to the plate center. Consider the same post shifted 0.13 m in the perpendicular plan direction, with its top still at the plate underside. Its true axis-aligned overlap is 0.18 by 0.05 = 0.009 square metres. The helper computes (0.09 + 1.09 - 0.62) * (0.09 + 0.09 - 0.13) = 0.028 square metres, above the caller's 0.014 threshold. The sampled bearing point at x=0.62 lies 0.13 m from the post center, inside its 0.09 m half-width plus the caller's 0.12 m tolerance; the role and vertical checks can also be satisfied. Exact rational arithmetic illustrates the source expressions, not native f32 execution.
candidates.safeguards: The caller also requires two plates, complete support references, a grounded bearing graph, roof-to-plate contact and valid points at both ends; other building audits can report separate issues. This witness does not establish that a supported generated plan has the shifted post, that the whole audit returns no issues, that the roof fails, or that the acceptance threshold is a complete structural model. The existing source assertions exercise zero overlap, a much larger post displacement and height changes; they were read but not run. Current Position, Radians and CuboidDimensions admit the finite coordinates, zero yaw and positive sizes, but whole-plan state admission remains open.
